title: Alibi and Autopsy Revisited
premise: Ulyana Reyes, a night-shift taxi dispatcher who has quietly catalogued two decades of the town's secrets, receives a prepaid commission from a nervous stranger: prove that Aldous Merrick will not be murdered on October 14th — a murder that, according to every official record and every resident's memory, already happened twenty years ago. Digging through her dispatch logs, Ulyana discovers that the original 'closed' case was manufactured by the town's founding family to bury an inconvenient death, and that her own missing sister was the last person to see the victim alive. As the anniversary approaches, Ulyana must reconstruct the true night from cab receipts, radio chatter, and unreliable memories, while someone begins erasing the records she depends on. In the end she exposes the conspiracy at a public inquest, learns her sister is alive but complicit in hiding, and chooses to file the truth where no one can alphabetize it away.
about_author: Emrys Hartwell is the pen name of a former small-town court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. Hartwell writes mysteries about people whose jobs give them front-row seats to other lives.

chapters.title: The Prepaid Fare
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On a slow night shift, a cash envelope arrives with instructions: prevent a murder scheduled for October 14th, signed by a client identified only as 'A.M.' Ulyana almost files it as a prank until she recognizes the date and the name Aldous Merrick — the man the whole town knows died twenty years ago. Beat: uneasy curiosity.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She introduces her private archive of dispatch logs, fare records, and overheard confessions, revealing how much of the town's history passes through her switchboard. The Merrick file is conspicuously thin — one night, then silence. Beat: quiet pride curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Man Who Died Twice
chapters.summary: Ulyana visits the county records office and finds Merrick's death certificate, autopsy report, and closed-case ruling all immaculate — too immaculate, filed by the same clerk within forty-eight hours. The coroner who signed it retired rich. Beat: first real dread.

chapters.title: Ghost Passenger
chapters.summary: Driver Marisol's POV. A veteran cabbie recalls picking up a fares-dodger near the Merrick estate on old anniversaries, always the same route, never the same face. She gives Ulyana a torn receipt with a partial license plate. Beat: superstitious unease turning practical.

chapters.title: The Founding Family's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Research into the Voss family, town patriarchs whose fortune built the courthouse and the taxi company itself. Ulyana realizes her employer answers to them. The prepaid envelope's watermark matches Voss stationery. Beat: betrayal.

chapters.title: A Sister Who Answers No Radio
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Flashback thread opens: her sister Katya vanished nineteen years ago, officially a runaway. Ulyana finds Katya's name on the Merrick case witness list — redacted. Beat: grief reawakened.

chapters.title: Interview with a Closed Case
chapters.summary: Retired Detective Hollis's POV. Hollis, dying of emphysema, admits he was ordered to close the Merrick investigation in three days. He kept one thing back: a photograph of tire tracks that don't match any registered vehicle. Beat: guilt seeking absolution.

chapters.title: October 13th, Again
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She maps the original night using dispatch timestamps and discovers a fifteen-minute gap in the radio log — deliberately spliced. Someone inside the company did it. Beat: the hunt turns inward.

chapters.title: The Client Calls
chapters.summary: Phone-call chapter, Ulyana listening. The disguised voice warns her off, then contradicts itself by paying a second installment. Voice analysis suggests a woman who has practiced sounding like a man. Beat: manipulation and intrigue.

chapters.title: Voss House Rules
chapters.summary: Matriarch Odile Voss's POV. Odile reviews the family's arrangement with the coroner and clerk, coldly assessing whether Ulyana Reyes is a threat or a tool. She orders surveillance. Beat: power exercised without conscience.

chapters.title: Night Shift Surveillance
chapters.summary: Ulyana notices a car idling across from the depot three nights running. She feeds it false routes through her dispatcher screen, confirming it reports to the Voss estate. Beat: cat-and-mouse confidence.

chapters.title: The Autopsy That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ulyana tracks down the original pathologist's assistant, now a hospice nurse, who confesses the body was never positively identified as Merrick — dental records were substituted. Whose body was it? Beat: the ground shifts.

chapters.title: Katya's Route
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Reconstructing Katya's last known movements, Ulyana finds her sister worked as a Voss housekeeper the year of the murder. The redacted witness statement's phrasing matches Katya's handwriting samples Ulyana keeps in a shoebox. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Marisol's Debt
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Pressured by a Voss lawyer to forget the ghost passenger, Marisol instead hands Ulyana twenty years of anniversary-night fare logs she kept out of spite. Pattern: pickups at a disused quarry roadhouse. Beat: solidarity.

chapters.title: The Quarry Roadhouse
chapters.summary: Ulyana breaks into the derelict roadhouse and finds a room preserved like a shrine: men's clothing, medicine bottles, newspapers up to nine years ago. Someone lived here long after Merrick 'died.' Beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: Alive, Then
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. If Merrick lived hidden for years, the murder being 'prevented' on October 14th means he's still alive — and someone plans to finish the job properly this time. The client isn't preventing a murder; they're outsourcing its confirmation. Beat: reversal.

chapters.title: Hollis's Photograph
chapters.summary: Hollis's POV. Dying, Hollis gives Ulyana the tire-track photo and names the vehicle: a Voss orchard truck. He asks her to put his confession on the record after he's gone. Beat: passing the torch.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: Ulyana arrives at the depot to find her archive ransacked — the Merrick file gone, her backup tapes wiped, her terminal logged under her own credentials. Inside job. Beat: violation and fury.

chapters.title: Rebuilding From Memory
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Stripped of records, Ulyana does what she's done for twenty years: remembers. She reconstructs key entries from recall, testing herself against Marisol's independent logs. Beat: identity as method — memory as evidence.

chapters.title: Odile Summons Her
chapters.summary: Tea at Voss House. Odile offers Ulyana a promotion, a raise, and gentle threats wrapped in courtesy, revealing she knows about the envelope. Ulyana accepts the meeting and gives away nothing. Beat: duel of composure.

chapters.title: The Second Envelope
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A new payment arrives with a change of instruction: 'Stop asking who. Ask why October 14th.' Ulyana cross-references the date and finds it's the Voss patriarch's birthday — the man whose deathbed confession Odile has spent decades containing. Beat: motive surfaces.

chapters.title: What the Patriarch Confessed
chapters.summary: Lawyer Bram Voss's POV. Odile's son Bram reveals the family secret in fragments: the old man killed his business partner Merrick Sr., and the 'murder' twenty years ago was staged to explain a second disappearance — Merrick Jr., who witnessed it as a boy. Beat: generational rot exposed.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Walls
chapters.summary: Ulyana deduces Merrick Jr. hid in plain sight, moving between the roadhouse and sympathetic households, fed by whoever sent the envelopes. The handwriting on the instructions finally clicks: it mirrors Katya's. Beat: heart-stopping recognition.

chapters.title: Sister, Stranger
chapters.summary: Katya's POV. Katya, living under another name in the next county, has been protecting Merrick Jr. for two decades and paying Ulyana to act without knowing — believing distance kept her safe. Now the Vosses have found him. Beat: love entangled with deception.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Depot
chapters.summary: Sisters meet at 3 a.m. amid dead phone lines. Anger, then the whole story: the staged murder, the bought autopsy, the years of hiding. Katya begs Ulyana to let it stay buried. Ulyana refuses. Beat: rupture.

chapters.title: October 12th
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Two days left. Ulyana lays out everything on her kitchen wall: timeline, gaps, players. One entry doesn't fit — a cab dispatched to the quarry at midnight on the 13th, driver unnamed. Beat: tightening coil.

chapters.title: The Unnamed Driver
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Under pressure, Marisol admits the midnight runs were hers — paid by young Merrick himself, who used her cab to collect his mail and medicine. He trusted her. She never knew why. Beat: loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Bram's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bram Voss privately contacts Ulyana: he wants the truth out too, to break his mother's grip, and offers the original death certificate forgery chain. But his price is immunity for the family's crimes. Beat: corrupt ally, tempting offer.

chapters.title: Refusal in Writing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana declines Bram's deal and instead mails certified copies of her reconstructed archive to the state attorney general, a journalist, and — pointedly — the county courthouse bulletin board. Beat: irrevocable commitment.

chapters.title: They Come for Katya
chapters.summary: Katya's POV. Voss security detains Katya, searching for Merrick. She stalls them with misdirection learned from twenty years of hiding, buying hours, and gets one smuggled message out via a delivery driver. Beat: terror and resourcefulness.

chapters.title: The Message Decoded
chapters.summary: Ulyana reads Katya's coded note: 'He goes to the water when cornered. Quarry lake. Midnight.' Ulyana realizes the Vosses let the message out deliberately — bait to draw both fugitives in. Beat: trap recognized too late to avoid.

chapters.title: Midnight Dispatch
chapters.summary: Ulyana uses her dispatcher authority to flood the Voss security channel with fake cab traffic, covering Marisol's drive to the quarry. For once, the switchboard is a weapon. Beat: competence as heroism.

chapters.title: The Water When Cornered
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge at the quarry lake: Merrick Jr. at the shore, Odile's men closing in, Katya breaking free, Ulyana arriving with a recording device live. Odile orders it finished 'cleanly.' Beat: brink of violence.

chapters.title: Everything on the Record
chapters.summary: Climax. Ulyana steps into the open, announces she is broadcasting to the attorney general's line, and plays Hollis's posthumous confession plus Bram's recorded admission. Odile's men falter; Bram turns on his mother publicly. Merrick walks out of the dark alive. Beat: truth as weapon.

chapters.title: Aftermath at the Inquest
chapters.summary: Ulyana testifies at the reopened inquest, her memory pitted against official records — and winning, because Marisol's logs corroborate every line. Odile is indicted; the coroner's exhumation order is signed. Beat: vindication, hard-won.

chapters.title: What Memory Owes
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Katya reconcile imperfectly. Katya explains her silence as protection; Ulyana names what it cost. They don't fully forgive, but they choose each other going forward. Beat: bruised reconciliation.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Drawer
chapters.summary: Epilogue-investigation. The retired clerk, facing charges, trades one last secret: the original body buried as Merrick Jr. was a John Doe from the quarry — meaning someone else died that night, uncounted. Ulyana takes the case. Beat: the work continues.

chapters.title: Filing the Truth
chapters.summary: Ulyana rebuilds her archive, but changes its system: nothing alphabetical anymore, nothing easy to erase — copies scattered among people who care. The town's secrets now have witnesses, not just a filing clerk. Beat: transformation of purpose.

chapters.title: New Shift, New Number
chapters.summary: Quiet denouement. Ulyana returns to the night shift, answering calls, a new prepaid envelope already on her desk — different handwriting, different town. She smiles, pours coffee, and picks up the phone. Beat: the dispatcher rides again.

chapters.title: Alibi and Autopsy, Revised Edition
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ulyana's reflective POV. She writes the full account we've just read, titling it as a correction to the official record, and mails the only copy to Merrick Jr., now free, letting him decide whether the past stays published. Some cases close; the truth stays open. Beat: peace earned, mystery honored.
